clue.text: Sleazy bars a rich man used

definitions.meaning: The name traditionally used for the rich man in the parable of Lazarus (Luke 16), from the Latin for rich

explanation.surface: A wealthy man frequents seedy drinking dens.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedy bar is a dive; and the Latin word for wealthy became the customary name of the rich man in the Gospel parable.

clue.text: I clued "bed" badly, it's to be inferred

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together poorly and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter admits a poor clue for 'bed', whose meaning must be guessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deducible means able to be worked out or inferred from evidence.

clue.text: Sign showing end of pier in Spanish port

indicators.note: in means the end letter goes inside the port's name

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of pier

explanation.surface: A signpost at the end of a jetty in a Spanish harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: One makes deceptive amounts of money

definitions.text: One makes deceptive amounts of money

parts.words: One makes deceptive amounts of money
parts.note: read as a coin-maker producing fake sums, it means a cheat who makes money by deceit

explanation.definitionFit: A swindler is a cheat who obtains money by fraud and deception.

clue.text: Checked, as deleted recordings sometimes were

definitions.meaning: held back or restrained, as feelings are
vinyl records withdrawn from the catalogue were sometimes pressed again, reissued

explanation.surface: Records quietly suppressed by a censor, some later revived.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as RE-PRESSED: a deleted record (one taken out of the catalogue) might be pressed again.
explanation.definitionFit: Repressed means held in check or restrained; split as re-pressed it means pressed a second time, like a reissued record.

clue.text: Fashion a poetic response to dying light?

definitions.meaning: a craze or the latest fashion

definitions.text: a poetic response to dying light?
definitions.meaning: Dylan Thomas wrote '..., ... against the dying of the light'

explanation.surface: Styling a verse that reacts to sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all the rage is the current fashion; and Dylan Thomas urged his father to fury against the dying of the light.

clue.text: Peppery old officer in film, presenting attractive image

indicators.note: in means the other pieces go inside the word for film

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
hot means spicy or peppery
Gen is short for General

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered veteran general in a movie looks good on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Photogenic means looking attractive in photographs.

clue.text: There's always a way in to this festival

indicators.note: in to signals the second pieces go into the word for always

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A saying that there is always a route into the celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival of the Resurrection.

clue.text: Press employee to omit last of common taxonomic groups

parts.note: a sub is a subeditor on a newspaper

indicators.note: to omit last of means the final letter of the word for common is dropped

parts.note: general means common or widespread

explanation.surface: A journalist is told to leave out the last of some ordinary classifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Subgenera are biological classification ranks between genus and species.

clue.text: Spoke at length, identifying detective originally on beat

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of detective

parts.note: to welt is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: A constable lectured at length about the officer who began on the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' suggests a policeman's round; it is the verb to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell on a topic is to speak or write about it at length.

clue.text: Corrupt party behind duke's intrepid action

indicators.note: the corrupt party comes behind, after, the duke's letter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
erring means straying morally, so corrupt
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A shady political party backs a nobleman's daring venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is heroic, daring deeds: bold and intrepid action.

clue.text: Fur that's fit to wear, though not posh

indicators.note: though not signals that the posh letter is left out of the word for fit to wear

parts.note: usable means fit for use, here fit to be worn
U is the crossword letter for upper-class or posh

explanation.surface: A fur coat good enough to wear, if not exactly smart.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'upper-class' is a British convention (U and non-U speech).
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the costly fur of a small Siberian marten-like animal.

clue.text: Democrat gloats about huge turnout?

indicators.note: about signals that the word for gloats goes round the Democrat's letter

parts.note: to crow is to boast or gloat

explanation.surface: A politician boasts of a massive attendance at a rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowds are large gatherings of people, which is what a huge turnout produces.

clue.text: Composition cleric held to be let-down

indicators.note: held signals that the composition contains the cleric

parts.note: a nonet is a musical composition for nine players
Ven is short for Venerable, the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A clergyman finds a piece of music disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ven. (Venerable) is the title given to an archdeacon in the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-event is something hyped that proves an anticlimax, a let-down.

clue.text: Elected representative's firm in Scotland's very badly run

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: in means the word for badly goes inside the Scots word for very

parts.note: unco is Scots for very or extremely
ill means badly
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A council member's business in Scotland is said to be very poorly managed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's 's stands for 'is'. UNCO is Scots for 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: A councillor is a member elected to a local council, so an elected representative.

clue.text: Greatly impressed, made several deliveries

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to bowl an over is to send down six balls in succession

explanation.surface: A postman astonished at how many parcels went out.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six deliveries bowled by one bowler from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bowled over is being astounded; in cricket, a bowler who bowled an over sent down six balls.

clue.text: Without oxygen we depart in forlorn state

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word we goes around oxygen

parts.note: taken as written
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
begone is an old command to go away, depart

explanation.surface: Short of oxygen, we leave in a miserable condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking'; here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Woebegone means looking sad and dejected, a forlorn condition.

clue.text: Robert or Gerard, possibly, taken in by another boy

indicators.note: taken in by signals letters held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Two men's names absorbed into a third lad's.
explanation.walkthrough: The names look like the boys; they are plants. 'Taken in by' finds the run inside 'another boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb Robert is a wild geranium and Herb Gerard is ground elder, so each is an example of a wild plant with medicinal uses.

clue.text: Person whose charges involve social workers

definitions.text: Person whose charges involve social workers

parts.words: Person whose charges involve social workers
parts.note: the charges are the creatures looked after, and the social workers are insects living in a colony, not welfare staff

explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper tends bees, which are social insects whose workers do the hive's labour.

clue.text: Drive away duck circling island lake

indicators.note: circling means the word for duck goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to duck is to dodge

explanation.surface: Chasing off a bird that circles a lake island.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to force out or drive away from a position.

clue.text: Still divisible by two

definitions.meaning: used as in '... better', meaning yet or still more
an ... number divides exactly by two

explanation.definitionFit: Even means yet, as in even better; and an even number divides exactly by two.

clue.text: Foresee tape being mislaid by worker here in Paris

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect
ici is French for here

indicators.note: being mislaid suggests the letters of tape are put in the wrong places

explanation.surface: A clerk in a French office predicts a reel of tape will go missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here in Paris' asks for the French word, and 'by' is only a link joining the worker to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate is to expect or foresee something before it happens.

clue.text: Voltaire's work lacks finish, to be honest

indicators.note: lacks finish means the final letter of the title is dropped

parts.note: Candide is Voltaire's satirical novel

explanation.surface: Voltaire's book feels incomplete, frankly.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and honest.

clue.text: Like the treatment of a noted subject

definitions.text: Like the treatment of a noted subject

parts.words: Like the treatment of a noted subject
parts.note: a subject written in musical notes is a theme, and developing it is the composer's treatment; the surface suggests handling a famous topic

explanation.definitionFit: Thematic means relating to a theme, the melodic subject a composer treats and develops.

clue.text: Snares used by jazz drummers?

definitions.meaning: old jazz slang for a drum kit

explanation.surface: Snare drums played in a jazz band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snares' suggests snare drums; the first sense is devices for catching animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Traps are devices for catching animals; in jazz, 'the traps' is the drum kit.

clue.text: Declare supporter is limited by drink

indicators.note: is limited by means the supporter is enclosed by the drink

parts.note: ale is beer
a leg is something that supports, as a table's does

explanation.surface: A fan says his loyalty only goes as far as the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or declare something, usually without proof.

clue.text: Some were put out by this article disturbing queen

definitions.text: Some were put out by this

indicators.note: disturbing means the letters of the article are jumbled

parts.note: the is the definite article
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A newspaper article upsetting the monarch angered some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests annoyed; it means made unconscious. 'Disturbing' rearranges THE to ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic used to make patients unconscious.

clue.text: Roman historian sporting, guild uniform without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation is removed from the uniform's name

parts.note: livery is the distinctive dress of a City of London guild
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: A Roman writer wearing a trade guild's uniform without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: Livy (Titus Livius) wrote the history of Rome from its foundation.

clue.text: Permitted to speak out

indicators.note: to speak signals that the word for permitted is said, giving a soundalike

parts.note: allowed means permitted

explanation.surface: Being given leave to voice one's views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speak out' looks like a phrase; 'out' alone is the definition, as in reading out.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloud means audibly, as in out loud: reading something out is reading it aloud.

clue.text: One brought in fat packet, say, for position up north

indicators.note: brought in means one is placed inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat
I is the Roman numeral for one
a packet (packet boat) is an example of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone receives a fat pay packet for a post in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAIRD is a Scottish landowner, hence 'up north'; a packet was a mail ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairdship is the rank or estate of a laird, the Scottish landed proprietor, so a position in Scotland.

clue.text: Person advancing in cunning, though in inadequate way

indicators.note: in means the person advancing goes inside the word for cunning

parts.note: sly means cunning
a lender advances money

explanation.surface: Someone getting ahead by guile, but not doing it well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advancing' suggests making progress; it means lending money.
explanation.definitionFit: Slenderly means in a slight or meagre manner, so inadequately.

clue.text: Bloomer gets formidable type beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a terror is a frightening or formidable person

explanation.surface: A gardener's flower falls foul of a fearsome sort with an axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a flower; it is the British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is informal British for a blunder or mistake.
